subject: Renewal: Resync monthly commit & 8→16 GPU expansion
messages:
From: Sam Reynolds <sam@skylabs.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts <contracts@skylabs.ai>
Date: 2027-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Upcoming renewal — exploring a 2x reserved pool increase

Hi Tessa,

Hope you’re doing well. Our Skylabs infra team has reviewed Q2 usage and we’re projecting a sustained increase in peak throughput for our inference workloads. Current committed pool: 8 dedicated GPUs (monthly commit). We’d like to explore doubling to 16 GPUs at renewal and understand the updated monthly commit profile, billing cadence, and any SLA/throughput guarantees we can attach.

Key asks from our side:
- A ballpark delta in monthly commit cost for 8→16 (we can share exact numbers offline)
- Estimated timeline to activate 16 GPUs (staged activation accepted)
- Ops guardrails (throughput QA, warmup/backfill plan, ramp cadence)
- Any impact on our current price tier or overage rules

I’ve attached a short usage export (skylabs_q2_usage_summary.csv) so you can see our token/embedding distribution. Can we set a short sync this week? Laura from Contracts is CC’d to flag timing for procurement.

Thanks,
Sam
Director of ML Infra
Skylabs AI

Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal — exploring a 2x reserved pool increase

Hi Sam — thanks for the export, that’s helpful context.

Short answer: we can absolutely support a staged activation from 8 → 16 GPUs at renewal and put throughput guardrails into the SLA. To get you an accurate monthly commit delta I’ll loop in Marissa (your AM) for pricing and Jonas for the activation playbook.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa will run a quick pricing comparison (8 vs 16) and provide two options: straight multiply vs blended phasing for month 1–3.
2) Jonas will sketch an ops cutover: warm cache strategy, KV prefill, and peak-window throttles so the expansion doesn’t cause cold-cache latency spikes.
3) We’ll put a two-week activation window in the contract with a go/no-go milestone tied to a small ramp test.

Can you confirm the preferred go-live target (end of Aug vs mid-Sept)? Also, if procurement prefers a single PO vs staged billing, flag that and Laura can coordinate with our billing team.

I’m happy to do a 30-minute call today or tomorrow to align.

—Tessa
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal — exploring a 2x reserved pool increase

Hi team — I ran two quick pricing scenarios and attached the lightweight sketch. Highlights:

- Option A (Immediate double): 2x monthly commit — list price × 2, 10% volume discount applied to incremental GPUs when signed at renewal.
- Option B (Phased ramp): Month 1–2 at +50% commit (12 GPUs billable), Month 3 onward at 16 GPUs; effective blended rate ~ 1.5× for first two months then ×2 after. Lower nearterm cash outlay and gives us runway for activation testing.
- SLA addendum: we can include a throughput SLA that guarantees 95th percentile sustained token throughput for pre-agreed peak-window sizes; remedy is credits rather than immediate termination.

I’ll prepare a clean PO-ready quote if you confirm Option A or B.

Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-commit-options-8to16-2027-07.pdf (pricing scenarios)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam@skylabs.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-20T10:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal — exploring a 2x reserved pool increase

Sam / team — quick ops note from the implementation side.

We recommend the following staged activation playbook (high level):
- Week 0: Pre-provision 8 additional GPUs in a warm standby pool; we’ll pre-warm key model artifacts and KV caches from your sample traces.
- Week 1: Run a controlled ramp test (10% traffic to the expanded pool) during a low-impact window, measure latency and cache hit-rate.
- Week 2: Increase to 50% traffic, run throughput stability checks, and exercise scaling policies.
- Week 3: Full cutover to 16 GPUs with a rollback window of 48 hours.

Operational guardrails we’ll include in the addendum: guided cooldown, auto-fallback to the 8-GPU baseline on sustained error spikes, and an ops-runbook co-owned by Skylabs + Redwood.

I’ll draft a short activation SOW for sign-off once Marissa confirms pricing.

—Jonas
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Kim <laura.kim@skylabs.ai>

Date: 2027-07-21T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal — exploring a 2x reserved pool increase

Thanks — quick procurement note from Skylabs Contracts. We prefer Option B (phased ramp) because it smooths cash flow across Q3. Two items for the redlines: 1) a clause committing Redwood to provide activation support (on-call hours and designated runbook owner), and 2) explicit billing proration language for the partial-month ramp.

Also: can you provide an estimated final PO amount so our finance team can start prepping approvals? We aim to sign by 2027-08-12 to meet our internal cycle.

Regards,
Laura Kim
Head of Procurement, Skylabs AI
